hero.title: Discover the Art of Herbal Tea Preparation
hero.lead: Bring the goodness of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea to your restaurant, café or snack corner. Explore simple and versatile preparation methods for refreshing hot and cold herbal beverages.

intro.eyebrow: Herbal Tea Recipes for Restaurants & Snack Corners
intro.title: Bring Herbal Wellness to Your Beverage Menu
intro.quote: Some of our ISKCON temples have added Govind Madhav Herbal Tea and Ginger Tea to the beverages list in Govinda Restaurants or Snack Corners. I request you can also add.
intro.invite: We warmly invite restaurants, cafés, snack corners, hotels and Govinda Restaurants to include Govind Madhav Herbal Tea and Ginger Tea in their beverage menus.
intro.methods: The four preparation methods below need only milk or water, the tea and, for cold drinks, ice.

hot.title: Hot Herbal Tea Recipes
hot.lead: Discover different ways to prepare a warm and refreshing cup of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.

cold.title: Refreshing Cold Herbal Tea Recipes
cold.lead: Serve delicious and refreshing herbal beverages using Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.

hotMilk.title: Hot Tea Prepared in Milk
hotMilk.ingredients:
1 litre of pure milk.
1 litre of mixture consisting of 50% milk and 50% water, or adjust milk and water as per taste.
16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
hotMilk.steps:
Take 1 litre of pure milk.
Alternatively, prepare a mixture of 50% milk and 50% water.
Adjust the quantity of milk and water according to your preferred taste.
Add 16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
Boil for 3 minutes.
If the preparation has less tea strength than desired, you can add more tea.
You can boil again. It will not lose its taste; rather, it will become tastier.

hotWater.title: Hot Tea Without Milk
hotWater.ingredients:
1 litre of water.
16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
hotWater.steps:
Take 1 litre of water.
Add 16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
Boil for 3 minutes.
If the preparation has less tea strength than desired, you can add more tea.
You can boil again. It will not lose its taste; rather, it will become tastier.
hotWater.note: This preparation is suitable for customers who prefer a milk-free herbal beverage.

coldShake.title: Cold Tea Shake Prepared in Milk
coldShake.ingredients:
1 litre of pure milk.
16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
Ice cubes.
coldShake.steps:
Take 1 litre of pure milk.
Add 16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
Boil for 3 minutes.
Allow the preparation to cool.
Add ice and shake in a mixer blender jar.
Serve cold.
coldShake.tip: If the preparation has less tea strength than desired, you can add more tea. You can boil again without losing its taste.

iced.title: Iced Cold Tea Without Milk
iced.ingredients:
1/2 litre of water.
16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
Cold water.
Ice cubes.
iced.steps:
Take 1/2 litre of water.
Add 16 grams of Govind Madhav Herbal Tea or Ginger Tea.
Boil for 3 minutes.
Cool the preparation.
Add 1/2 litre of cold water.
Add ice and serve.
iced.tip: If the preparation has less tea strength than desired, you can add more tea. You can boil again without losing its taste.

menu.title: Make Herbal Tea a Part of Your Beverage Menu
menu.lead: Four ways to serve Govind Madhav Herbal Tea and Ginger Tea, each prepared with one of the recipes on this page.

hotHerbal.title: Hot Herbal Tea
hotHerbal.body: Govind Madhav Herbal Tea boiled for 3 minutes in milk, a milk and water mixture, or water alone.

hotGinger.title: Hot Ginger Tea
hotGinger.body: Govind Madhav Ginger Tea, prepared hot in milk or in water with the same 16 grams to a litre.

coldShake.title: Cold Herbal Tea Shake
coldShake.body: Boiled in pure milk, cooled, then shaken with ice in a mixer blender jar and served cold.

iced.title: Iced Herbal Tea
iced.body: Boiled in 1/2 litre of water, cooled, topped with 1/2 litre of cold water and served over ice.
